summary: Cilnidipine is a long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that blocks both L-type (vascular) and N-type (sympathetic nerve) calcium channels, used for hypertension. Typical dose is 5-10 mg once daily (max 20 mg). Dual N-type blockade reduces reflex tachycardia and pedal edema compared with conventional dihydropyridines and confers renoprotective effects (reduced proteinuria). It is marketed in Japan and India and is not FDA-approved.
indications: Adjunctive antihypertensive with renoprotective benefit (proteinuria reduction) in some regional guidelines

dosage.d: 5-10 mg once daily; usual maintenance 10 mg/day
May increase up to 20 mg once daily (maximum)

admin: Take orally once daily, usually after breakfast
Swallow whole with water; take at the same time each day
Do not stop abruptly without medical advice
Monitor blood pressure and heart rate during therapy
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness
moa: Cilnidipine is a dihydropyridine that inhibits transmembrane calcium influx through both L-type voltage-gated calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle and N-type calcium channels on sympathetic nerve endings. L-type blockade produces arterial vasodilation and lowers blood pressure, while N-type blockade suppresses presynaptic noradrenaline release, blunting reflex sympathetic activation. This dual action reduces reflex tachycardia and pedal edema and dilates both afferent and efferent renal arterioles, lowering glomerular pressure and proteinuria.
preg: Not recommended; safety in pregnancy is not established and dihydropyridines may cause maternal hypotension and reduced placental perfusion. Use only if the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk, with specialist supervision.
lact: Avoid; it is not known whether cilnidipine is excreted in human milk. If treatment is essential, discontinue breastfeeding.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is established; cilnidipine is largely hepatically metabolized. It dilates both afferent and efferent glomerular arterioles and may reduce proteinuria, but monitor renal function and blood pressure.
hepatic: Use with caution as cilnidipine is metabolized by the liver (CYP3A4); clearance may be reduced and plasma levels increased in hepatic impairment. Consider lower starting dose and monitor closely.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., azole antifungals, ritonavir) - increased cilnidipine exposure and hypotension
interactions.food: Grapefruit juice may increase plasma concentration (CYP3A4 inhibition); food may enhance absorption - take consistently with respect to meals.
interactions.alcohol: May potentiate hypotensive and dizziness effects; advise limiting intake.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory interference; monitor BP and renal parameters.

monitoring: Blood pressure at baseline and follow-up
Heart rate (assess for reflex tachycardia, typically minimal)
Renal function and urinary protein where renoprotection is intended
counsel: Take once daily after breakfast at the same time each day
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness; report fainting or palpitations
Do not stop the medicine suddenly without advice
Avoid grapefruit juice and limit alcohol
Report ankle swelling, severe headache, or yellowing of skin/eyes
pk: Antihypertensive effect within hours; full effect over days to weeks
Plasma peak approximately 2-3 hours after oral dose
Store below 25-30 C, protected from light and moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved; record pending clinical review.
Dual L/N-type blockade gives less reflex tachycardia and less pedal edema than amlodipine
N-type sympathetic blockade lowers noradrenaline release - favorable in sympathetic overactivity
Dilates both afferent and efferent renal arterioles - reduces proteinuria (renoprotective)
Marketed mainly in Japan and India; dose data from manufacturer/regional prescribing information
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule; do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause marked and prolonged hypotension, reflex tachycardia, and flushing. Management is supportive: place supine, give IV fluids, monitor cardiac and BP status; vasopressors and IV calcium may be used for refractory hypotension. Dialysis is unlikely to be helpful given high protein binding.
